changed.title: Some AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 5 gates represents one of two named 5 by 5 graphs (masks 16235582, 16236078) on the one-a-side promise
changed.statement:
∃ M ∈ ([16235582, 16236078] : List ℕ), ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 5 ∧
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 5 => M.testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) C
changed.unlocks: whether a NOT gate can save more than 2n - 5 gates on the one-a-side promise at side 5, on the two graphs the read-once count leaves open; a met step breaks the 2n - 5 pair there.
changed.context: No witness is known to us; this is a search; two NOT gates or an input read twice are possible here. Give a gate list of at most 5 AND, OR and NOT gates of fan-in two for one of the two masks, judged by evaluation on the 25 promise inputs. Each graph needs at least 11 gates without NOT gates (checked floors: the 'at most 10 AND/OR' rows read refuted). The other twenty masks of the first break step are covered by a separate 'none exists' form. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.

changed.title: Majority of 8 bits (at least 4 on) has an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 22 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.HasCircuitSize 8 (fun x : Fin 8 → Bool => decide (4 ≤ (List.ofFn x).count true)) 22
changed.unlocks: a first rung below our own bar for this function
changed.context: Answer with a circuit, not an argument: a gate list (operation, wires read; wires 0 to n-1 are the input bits in the order the statement names, gate j writes wire n+j, each gate reads only earlier wires) and the output wire. Judged by one kernel evaluation over every input. Any search method is welcome; only the circuit is checked. The rung at 26 is checked; we do not hold that circuit. We do not know whether 22 exists. If your circuit uses a NOT gate, say so.

changed.title: With the ordered pair and triple witness conditions, selecting a row after free column preprocessing needs 2n−1 AND/OR gates
changed.statement:
∀ (n m p : Nat) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (code : Fin m → Fin p → Bool)
    (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
  2 ≤ n →
  (∀ u v : Fin n, u ≠ v →
    ∃ c : Fin m, G u c = true ∧ G v c = false) →
  (∀ u v w : Fin n, u ≠ v → u ≠ w → v ≠ w →
    ∃ c : Fin m, G u c = true ∧ G v c = true ∧ G w c = false) →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C →
  (∀ (u : Fin n) (c : Fin m),
    C.eval (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => decide (i = u)) ++ List.ofFn (code c)) = G u c) →
  2 * n - 1 ≤ C.size
changed.unlocks: bounds the remaining row-selector gates when column preprocessing is free
changed.context: Fix the column code when comparing rows. With two incomparable rows both raw inputs matter and neither can feed the output directly. One shared initial gate treats them alike, so three gates are needed. Turning off a row saves two gates if it has two readers or its sole reader is AND. Otherwise count the private row ORs. Domination excludes a shared sole OR reader. A common column missed by a third excludes a shared sole AND reader. Charge two reader slots per row OR. The matching ceiling uses n free column predicates, n ANDs and n−1 ORs.

changed.title: The two-lit function of the graph H on 6 points with mask 281 on shared wires has an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 5 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 5 ∧ ∀ i j : Fin 6, C.eval (List.ofFn fun k : Fin 6 => decide (k = i ∨ k = j)) = (281 : ℕ).testBit (6 * min i.val j.val + max i.val j.val)
changed.unlocks: the exact size of the two-lit-points function of this graph on six shared wires; the family shows where a NOT gate pays with no equal lines
changed.sketch: We hold a circuit of 6 gates, a weak hand form (our best over a few orders of the points, repeated gates merged): OR(1,2), OR(5,6), NOT(7), AND(0,8), AND(1,2), OR(9,10) (inputs 0-5 are the 6 points, gate k is wire 6 + k, the output is the last gate). We hold no circuit of 5 gates; this is a search. A met unit may be a better order of the points and not a saving from a NOT gate. A proof exhibits 5 gates and evaluates the 21 inputs.

changed.title: An AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 24 gates computes the edge function of the listed graph on 14 vertices with 19 edges
changed.unlocks: one search on a named graph: is there a circuit one gate smaller than the best we know for its edge function; a found circuit is a bound from above, a proof of none a bound from below
changed.context: SKETCH: truth not known to us; the opposite row is offered beside it. Proved by exhibiting ONE circuit with at most the stated number of gates of fan-in at most two that computes the edge function (true exactly when both ends of some edge are true) on every input; checked by evaluation. The best circuit known to us has one gate more (computed, not checked). Size: minutes if such a circuit exists. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
